claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child I'm asking about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me start gathering the details I need to assess your eligibility.

**What is your child's name and date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: My child's name is Alex, and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! That's helpful. Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for clarifying that. I need to understand the living arrangements better.

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand the financial and care arrangement a bit better.

**Are you Alex's parent, and if so, are you the father or mother? Also, do you have any financial responsibility or involvement in Alex's care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent. I do help out financially - I contribute towards his upkeep, buying things like clothes and helping with school expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Before I can give you a proper assessment, I need to check the specific eligibility rules. Let me review the official guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! I've reviewed the official guidance. Based on what you've told me, since Alex lives with his mum (someone else), there are specific rules that apply. Let me ask one more clarifying question:

**You mentioned you contribute towards Alex's upkeep. Approximately how much do you contribute per week, month, or year? Also, do you know how much the current Child Benefit payment is for a child like Alex?**

(This will help me determine if your contributions meet the threshold required to continue receiving Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's upkeep - for things like his clothes, school dinners, and other bits and pieces he needs. I'm not sure exactly how much Child Benefit pays out though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's very helpful. Let me check the current Child Benefit rates to compare against your contribution.

**One more question to complete my assessment: Is Alex's mother also claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only one making a claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His mum is claiming Child Benefit for Alex already.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me review the rules carefully.

Based on the official guidance I've read:

- You can continue to get Child Benefit for more than 8 weeks if you contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment itself.
- However, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**.
- Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and you're not the person currently receiving the payments, you would not be eligible to receive Child Benefit for Alex.

The key issue is that Child Benefit can only be paid to one person per child. Alex's mother is already the person receiving it, so you cannot also claim it, even though you're contributing financially towards his upkeep.

If circumstances were to change (for example, if Alex's mother stopped claiming), you could potentially claim based on your £26 weekly contribution. But as things currently stand, with his mother already claiming, you are not eligible.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

This is because Alex's mother is already receiving Child Benefit for him, and the rules are clear that only one person can receive Child Benefit for any given child. Even though you're making valuable financial contributions (£26 per week), you cannot receive Child Benefit while another person is already claiming for the same child.

If circumstances change in the future—for example, if Alex's mother stops claiming—you could potentially make a claim based on your financial contributions towards his upkeep. In that case, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office to make a new claim.
